Subject: Re: Commercial choreography — order form redlines & invoicing approach

Amelia / Camila — thanks for the context and the tax cert. Short answers from legal/ops:

- Reverse-charge: we can accept the reverse-charge wording conditionally. Required items: (a) the BlueBay tax certificate on file (received), (b) the invoice must include the line "reverse-charge applies" and the BlueBay VAT id, and (c) Redwood will not gross-up for withholding where reverse charge applies. If a withholding (third-country) scenario arises, we’ll need to re-open.

- Net terms: we are open to a 45-day payment term for the first 12 months subject to two guardrails for accounting: (1) Redwood issues the initial activation invoice Net 30 for the onboarding fee, and (2) recurring invoices can be batched monthly but paid Net 45. If BlueBay requests Net 45 for all invoices including activation, we need a one-time credit holdback clause (2.5% of first-month invoice) to offset the timing gap.

Draft language we suggest adding to the order form: a short paragraph under "Payment and Taxes" that captures the reverse-charge acceptance + the 12-month Net 45 concession with the holdback mechanism.

I’ll paste the proposed clause below so procurement can review quickly.

--- Proposed clause (suggested insertion):
"If Customer provides a valid VAT/tax certificate evidencing reverse-charge eligibility, Redwood will issue invoices reflecting the applicable reverse-charge treatment. Customer shall include the Customer VAT number on all invoices. For the initial 12-month period, Redwood will accept Net 45 payment terms for recurring charges provided that (i) activation/onboarding fees remain Net 30, and (ii) Redwood may apply a one-time holdback equal to 2.5% of the first invoice amount to mitigate cashflow timing differences. The holdback will be returned or applied to the final invoice of the 12-month period subject to account standing."

Camila — if that matches the commercial intent, Ben can propose the financial tradeoffs to BlueBay (discount vs holdback).

Kim
Head of Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Commercial choreography — order form redlines & invoicing approach

Amelia — appreciate the patience. Picking up Kim's clause and Camila's ask, here's a pragmatic commercial option that keeps BlueBay at Net 45 while protecting Redwood cashflow:

Option A (preferred, minimal customer impact):
- Activation/onboarding fee: invoiced Net 30.
- Recurring usage: invoiced monthly, paid Net 45.
- One-time holdback: 2.5% of month-1 recurring invoice to be released at month-12 if account is in good standing.
- As a courtesy, Redwood will extend a 0.5% one-time credit against month-2 invoice to offset the holdback impact.

Option B (if holdback not acceptable to customer):
- Redwood maintains Net 30 for all invoices OR
- Customer agrees to a modest prepay structure for the first two quarters (50% prepay of estimated consumption) to enable Net 45 on the balance.

If BlueBay confirms Option A we can update the order form and legal can accept the reverse-charge insertion. Camila — if you’re comfortable I’ll send a short note to procurement with the two options and ask them to pick.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
